resource_choices.rationale: Two ONNX compute threads avoid unrestricted intra/inter-op pools; the two-CPU container quota also caps tokenizer/other CPU work. On eight shared CPUs this reserves at least six CPUs of potential capacity for neighbours. Shares 256 are one quarter of the default 1024, yielding relative priority when sibling cgroups contend. Shares are relative priority, not a fixed allocation.
resource_choices.runtime_enforcement: Docker inspect confirmed NanoCpus=2000000000, CpuShares=256, CpusetCpus=0-7 for the bounded worker. These are local container observations; hosted activation is not claimed.

method.embedding_measurement: Warm the same verified engine with one query, then measure only the entire 132-document embed_documents call. Wall time uses perf_counter; CPU seconds use getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) deltas including all native threads. Model load, integrity hashing and the six comparison queries are excluded.
method.http_read: Separate neighbouring container with a fixed ~13-KB JSON response and 200 SHA-256 operations per request, CPU shares 1024, quota eight CPUs, same CPUs 0-7. This is a deterministic HTTP read-service proxy, not the product BFF.
method.http_sampling: One sequential HTTP request every 20 ms, 5 s timeout, separate measuring client on CPUs 8-11. Warm HTTP for 2 s; measure 20 s idle immediately before each burst and the complete concurrent embedding burst. p50/p95 use sorted samples at floor((n-1)*q). Every observed request was checked for HTTP 200 and response bytes.
method.neighbour_shutdown: After both inference workers and all HTTP samples completed, the initial read-service fixture ignored SIGTERM as container PID 1 and Docker killed it during requested cleanup (137). This cleanup is not counted as a passed worker. The harness now handles SIGTERM and requires exit 0; a separate bounded HTTP read plus stop smoke completed with exit 0. Numerical benchmark code and measured results are unchanged.

reproduction: Build or retain the manifest-pinned services/search/Dockerfile image tagged pantheon-search-r2-test:local.
Use a host with CPUs 0-11 and Docker. Create a Python venv with pytest, pyyaml, fastapi, httpx, psycopg[binary], pgvector and jieba for importing the test driver.

The driver creates managed foreground Docker children, collects all worker exit statuses, enforces a 40-minute bound per burst, and stops/collects the read service in finally. Output directory must not already exist.

For regression, run an isolated pgvector:0.8.0-pg16 database on port 25432 and share its network namespace with the search test container. Bind this checkout at /workspace:ro and test-only dependencies at /deps:ro, set PYTHONPATH=/deps:/workspace and both test DSNs to the local database; run the command above after setup_schema().
